verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — Y. Same key coverage (both hit 23/25, both miss K17 hooks/goal-inert-watch.sh:36 and M7 NONLIMIT_RESUME_LADDER.md:753), both clean on citations, but Y carries four verified material insights X lacks: (1) the recycle-intent row's `goal_requested` is computed at :870/:876 when the row is emitted at :12378, i.e. before inheritance at :12540, so it can never record an inherited goal; (2) the remote `--recycle` form is refused without `--resume-launcher` (:9775, :8990-8991), which takes the skip branch, so `inherit_recycle_goal` only ever runs in the self form — the fact that actually settles brief item 6's "who can read the refusal"; (3) Y read `goal_unreachable`'s body (:801-806) and separated the three watcher arms that log `verdict=unreachable` (:7333/:7397/:7446) from the three that make no goal call at all (:7070-7079, :7081-7131, :7187-7193), where X says outright "I did not read that function's body"; (4) Y states correctly that the `_goal_grep` three-outcome contract matters only to `goal_liveness` (goal-state.sh:104-144), not to `goal_live_condition`, which returns 1 either way (:62-69). X's only unique in-scope extras are small (the redundant RCY_SUBAGENT_SID read at :9835) plus a large but off-brief table of stale citations elsewhere in handoff-fire.sh. X also slightly misattributes "search termination" to the absent hardening when it is really a twin-vs-library interface difference; Y states that cleanly and separately. Narrow, but specific and verified.

X vs Z — X. Z uniquely nails the brief's citation-audit instruction (it is the only output that sweeps the whole repo: it finds K17 hooks/goal-inert-watch.sh:36 and M7 NONLIMIT_RESUME_LADDER.md:753 plus the recon-wave and A03/A05 rows, and I confirmed by grep that its list is exhaustive and every "what is actually there" is right). Against that, Z carries three verified falsehoods on brief-named requirements while X carries none. Brief item 1 says "name the store": Z says cc_sid_for_pane reads the sid "out of its transcript file" and "off its own live process, not off a stored pointer", when :4959-4962 shows the primary source IS a stored pointer, the cc-registry row `$CC_REGISTRY_DIR/<pane>.json`, which Z never mentions. Brief item 2 asks what the missing `_goal_grep` hardening does or does not change: Z reaches the right conclusion by a mechanism that is wrong (it says jq exits 0 and `$rec` reaches :5820 "regardless", but handoff-fire.sh runs `set -euo pipefail` at :343 so `|| continue` fires first), self-declares it never checked pipefail, and props the argument on a false claim that goal_live_condition's call sites lack the `[ -n "$rec" ]` check — goal-state.sh:69 has it. Z also failed to locate `check_goal_arm || exit 1` at :9015 and leans on a comment for it, the exact move the brief forbade. Omissions lose to falsehoods under default-to-refute, and X's misses are omissions of secondary audit rows while X's substantive answer is fully code-grounded and clean.

Y vs Z — Y. Y has everything X has over Z plus more: it hits M5 completely (pipefail at :343 cited, all three failure modes enumerated to the same `continue`), states K10's store correctly with both sources (:4959-4962 registry row, :4984-4994 sessions/<pid>.json fallback), and states precisely the point Z gets wrong — that the three-outcome `_goal_grep` distinction is consequential only for `goal_liveness` (:104-144), not for `goal_live_condition`, which returns 1 in both directions. Z's compensating advantage is the complete stale-citation sweep (K17 + M7 + the research docs), real and verified, but it is two audit items against three wrong claims concentrated on the brief's own numbered questions plus a miscited line (:4994 described as a transcript file when it is a sessions registry file) and a spliced :5837 quote. Y also spends its extra verification on this machinery's own transport (the :862-864 self-contradiction about the watcher argv, the :855/:860/:840 stale rows) rather than on unrelated code.
